statement: For E_41 and p>=5 of good ordinary reduction, Castella's CM Theorem B reduces nonvanishing of its admissibly constructed generalized Kato class to p-primary Sha finiteness, using the known rank-two equality and nonzero localization. Five ordinary primes have explicit local parameter certificates.
hypotheses: Prior cycle-four analytic and rational rank certificates; CM by Z[i]; good ordinary p>=5; auxiliary characters satisfying (1.5) and Theorem A(i)-(ii) of Castella's paper.
definitions: Bloch-Kato Selmer group of V_pE; restriction to E(Q_p) completed and tensored Q_p; formal parameter -x/y; p-primary Sha.
source_locators: Castella, Generalised Kato classes on CM elliptic curves of rank 2, version Feb 13 2026, Theorem B, pp.4–5, https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~castella/Kato-Schoen.pdf; BSD-B004.
proof_or_gap: Rank two and Selmer exact sequence give dim Sel=2 iff Sha[p^infty] finite by cofinitely generatedness. A nontorsion rational point remains nontorsion locally, hence restriction is nonzero. Theorem B now gives equivalence, not a new finiteness proof. Local formal parameter digits independently test restriction.
implication_to_claim: Isolates an actual missing nonvanishing input for extending the rank comparison to odd p; conditional route only.
unproved_dependencies: Explicit admissible auxiliary character construction and independent generalized Kato class nonvanishing, or other independent p-primary Sha finiteness proof. Universal rank comparison remains open.
adversarial_findings: Nonzero localization is not sufficient without dimension two. Supersingular and bad primes fail the theorem setting; circular use of assumed Sha finiteness does not close the obligation.
